Actually, as long as the rock's movement is not impaired and it switches to using telefragging, the rock is rather slow (40 meters/hour at most, if I got the math correctly - it takes it a day to move a kilometer). So, yes, it will keep killing people for ever, but its slowness ensures that it will probably not exceed one person per day - which is a lot less than any other potential hazards, including the most mundane ones.
It's very deadly for the poor soul that it targeted, but not that much for humanity as a whole.

item.content:encoded:
And we are just assuming that 682 doesn't have a name. Because of the continued noncooperation from 682 we do not know much about the creature, at least from what I've seen.

It may be a possible route to take, as 260 appears to target the being that next comes in contact with the previous victim, either by killing the target, as in Scenario 3, or post mortem, Scenario 1.
The next course may be to put the current victim in the room with 682, have 682 do his standard operation around humans, while observing 260 to see what occurs next.
If 682 does adapt to 260, then it will either destroy 260, in a possible event such as developing an organ to destroy it specifically, or keep it occupied until the destruction of 682, in the event of thickening of the skin or similar action.
If 260 kills 682 then the only one who loses is the current target.
If 260 does not pick a new target, then 260 could be close to considered neutralized, or if not 682, then we just lost the one Agent, who already has a death sentence.
